question.worked_solution:
First, we note that $x=0$ cannot be a solution since this would make the denominator on the left-hand side zero.

We can flip an equation involving two fractions as follows:

$$
\frac{a}{b}=\frac{c}{d}\,⟹\,\frac{b}{a}=\frac{d}{c}
$$

The above technique works whenever $a$ and $c$ are both different from zero.

Therefore, we can flip the given equation as follows:

$$
-\frac{2x}{1}=\frac{5}{3}
$$

The above equation simplifies to

$$
-2x=\frac{5}{3}
$$

We can now solve this equation using the multiplication principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x & =\frac{5}{3} \\ (-\frac{1}{2})\cdot (-2x) & =(-\frac{1}{2})\cdot \frac{5}{3} \\ \cancel{(-\frac{1}{2})}\cdot (\cancel{-2}x) & =-\frac{5}{6} \\ x & =-\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
